judged_text: In sharing mode responseBody is the sync contract {access_token, expiry}, but the adapter consumes Webex-specific fields (refresh_token, expires_in) that this contract never contains. Under credential sync the Webex adapter persists a credential with undefined refresh_token and a NaN expiry, so meetings fail once the first access token expires and the credential can never be refreshed again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a “credential sync” mode via `refreshOAuthTokens`, which (per its comment) expects the sync endpoint response to “only contain the access token and expiry date” and returns the raw `fetch` `Response` from `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when enabled (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In the Webex adapter, the refresh flow was changed to use `refreshOAuthTokens` but still passes the returned `response` into `handleWebexResponse(response, credential.id)` (`packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`) and does not use the new `parseRefreshTokenResponse` helper that other adapters switched to. From the diff alone, this shows Webex has no adaptation for the minimal sync response shape, so in sync mode it will likely parse a non-Webex token shape with Webex-specific expectations, breaking refresh behavior. The specific downstream effects (undefined `refresh_token`, NaN expiry) are not directly shown in this diff, but the contract mismatch is.
